title: Compression stocking fitting
what: A specialist measures your legs and fits stockings, knee-highs, or tights in the right size and pressure level.
why: For varicose veins, leg swelling, after vein surgery, in pregnancy, or to prevent blood clots as your doctor prescribes.
tell_doctor: If you have a doctor's prescription, and which compression class
Any wounds or skin problems on your legs

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Best to come in the morning, before your legs swell.

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: If swelling is severe, you may be asked to lie with your legs raised before measuring.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that lets you uncover your legs up to the thigh.

bring: Your vein ultrasound, if you had one
steps: The specialist asks about your prescription and symptoms
The ankle, calf, and thigh are measured, and leg length too
The size and style are chosen from the measurements
You are shown how to put them on correctly
Sometimes you are offered a try-on
feel: The stockings feel tight at first. That is normal
after: Put the stockings on in the morning, while still in bed
Take them off at night, unless your doctor says otherwise
Hand wash them in warm water
Stockings are usually replaced every 4 to 6 months. They lose pressure
red_flags: Your toes turn blue, numb, or cold in the stockings: take them off and tell your doctor
Pain, wounds, or strong skin redness

faq.q: Can I buy stockings without being measured?
faq.a: Better not. The wrong size does not help and can sometimes harm.

faq.q: How can I put them on more easily?
faq.a: Turn the stocking inside out down to the heel, slip it on your foot, and smooth it upward. Rubber gloves and special aids help.

reminders.text: Compression stocking fitting tomorrow. Come in the morning, before your legs swell. Bring your doctor's prescription.
